summary: Sh. Ali Mashhour continues his discussion on the chapters of bathing from the book of purification in Al-Wajeez. He clarifies the distinction between conditions, pillars, obligations, and sunnahs in Islamic jurisprudence, emphasizing that these categories are scholarly tools for teaching rather than the basis of worship itself. Sh. Ali Mashhour explains that the two pillars of bathing (ghusl) are intention and complete washing of the entire body including the mouth and nose. He provides practical examples, such as a person who bathes without the intention of purification remaining in a state of janaba despite physically bathing, to illustrate why intention is essential for the validity of ritual purification.
